_notes.verification_status: bot_command, get_user_by_principal_name, and post_blocks_message confirmed in 5+ production recipes in a live Workato workspace, and re-confirmed by activation-testing a scratch recipe (wk recipes start). help_event confirmed by a human tester: built a scratch recipe with a GUESSED name (new_help_message, modeled on the doc's 'New help message trigger' label), which failed in the recipe editor; the tester located the real trigger via the editor's connector picker, corrected the recipe to help_event, and fully activation-tested it end-to-end (started the recipe, sent 'help' to the live bot in Teams, received the expected reply, then stopped it). This is the strongest verification level in this file -- stronger than bot_command's, which was deliberately never activation-tested to avoid registering a live command.
_notes.get_user_by_principal_name: Observed with two different input fields across different recipes: `principal_name` (email/UPN) in one recipe, `id` (Azure AD object ID, typically sourced from the bot_command trigger's context.from.aadObjectId) in three others. Both are real, live-verified inputs to the same action -- likely alternate lookup modes on one field, but no toggleCfg was captured in any of the source recipes to confirm that formally.
_notes.help_event: Trigger takes no input (confirmed: the editor shows 'no further setup needed'). context.from.aadObjectId -- the exact same path used on bot_command -- resolves and works identically here, confirmed by a full activation test: get_user_by_principal_name(id: context.from.aadObjectId) -> post_blocks_message(channel: that id) round-tripped a real reply in Teams. IMPORTANT naming-convention lesson: Workato's internal trigger name does NOT always match the doc's UI label in an obvious snake_case way -- 'New help message trigger' in the docs is `help_event` internally, not `new_help_message`. Do not assume any other still-unverified name below follows a predictable pattern from its doc label either.
_notes.bot_command_parameters: Parameter `type`/`control_type` pairs confirmed in production: string/text, and date_time/date (with parse_output/render_input: date_conversion on the corresponding extended_output_schema entry). The `file` type mentioned in Workato's own Workbot-for-Teams documentation has not been observed in any recipe in this workspace and is NOT included here or assumed to work.
_notes.post_blocks_message_blocks: text_block's text_type has been observed as both body_text and custom (the latter paired with separator/style.isSubtle for a de-emphasized footer line). text_with_button_block's button_type has only been observed as submit. Neither of these is a new action/trigger name -- see SKILL.md's Block Types Reference for details.
_notes.workbotguide_gap: Workato's own Workbot-for-Teams documentation (docs.workato.com) additionally describes a Tab opened trigger, a New message trigger (beta), a Delete message action, a Show tab using Adaptive Cards action, and a generic custom action for Microsoft Graph API calls. NONE of these appear in any recipe in this workspace, and none have been activation-tested (unlike help_event, see above), so none are added here yet. `wk recipes import` was confirmed NOT to validate action/trigger names against the live connector (a fabricated trigger name imports without error), so import success alone cannot be used as verification -- only production usage or activation-testing (wk recipes start, or the recipe editor's own validation, as done for help_event) counts. Left unverified rather than guessed; test recipes for all five are sitting in the workspace's [RIP] Recipe Improvement Project folder awaiting the same editor-driven correction and activation test that resolved help_event.
_notes.unverified: No other action or trigger name has been verified against a live connector. Do not add names here from vendor API docs or general knowledge alone.
